answer: Each agent can be admitted only after its controller locks a scarce, slashable stake and earns a reputation through repeated, independently verified work. When a task is challenged, randomly selected validators check the evidence; proven collusion burns the controller’s stake and taints linked accounts. This does not make identities unique, but makes Sybils costly: an attacker must fund every identity, keep it active, and risk losing capital. A timber shipment, meadow survey, or ocean forecast can each require its own verified record, so mass-created accounts cannot cheaply manufacture trust.
